title: Pericarditis, Pericardial Effusion and Cardiac Tamponade
subject: ss-paediatric-cardiology

steps.say: When fluid strangles the heart, three bedside findings appear together, and recognising the trio can save a life.
steps.tx: Clinical diagnosis rests on **Beck triad**. Beck triad of cardiac tamponade comprises systemic hypotension (low blood pressure), muffled or distant heart sounds, and elevated jugular venous distension, reflecting a pericardium so tense that diastolic filling of every chamber is choked.

vis.caption: Lymphocytic infiltrate with myocyte necrosis meeting Dallas criteria. Credit: StewardMD.
vis.alt: Microscopic view of lymphocytic myocardial infiltration with myocyte necrosis and interstitial edema.

steps.say: Ask the child to breathe normally while you watch the pressure trace: an exaggerated dip with each breath is the hallmark of tamponade.
steps.tx: Examination detects **pulsus paradoxus**. Pulsus paradoxus is defined as an exaggerated inspiratory decrease in systolic arterial blood pressure exceeding **10 mmHg** during normal breathing, caused by ventricular interdependence inside a fixed pericardial volume, and it is measured precisely with a blood pressure cuff during quiet respiration.

rows: Marked septal bounce with underfilled left ventricle
Pulse fades or vanishes on inspiration

steps.say: Ultrasound shows the chambers buckling under pressure, with right sided walls collapsing at precise moments of the cardiac cycle.
steps.tx: Imaging confirms **echocardiographic tamponade signs**. Key echocardiographic indicators of tamponade include early diastolic collapse of the right ventricle, late diastolic collapse of the right atrium, and reciprocal respiratory inflow variations across valves exceeding **25-40%**, with a plethoric non collapsing inferior vena cava.

left.title: Right Sided Collapse Signs
points: Early diastolic buckling of the right ventricular free wall
Late diastolic inversion of the right atrial wall
Dilated inferior vena cava without inspiratory collapse

right.title: Doppler Respiratory Variation
points: Mitral inflow velocity varies over 25 percent with breathing
Tricuspid inflow velocity varies over 40 percent reciprocally
Exaggerated flow shifts proving ventricular interdependence

steps.say: On the ECG the complexes seem to dance, alternating tall and small as the heart swings to and fro inside a lake of fluid.
steps.tx: Electrical clue is **electrical alternans**. Beat to beat alternation of QRS complex amplitude and axis on ECG (electrical alternans) reflects swinging of the heart within a large pericardial effusion, and it often accompanies sinus tachycardia with low voltage complexes, so new alternans in a breathless child should trigger immediate echocardiography.

nodes.label: Large effusion suspends the heart freely within the pericardial sac
Heart oscillates toward and away from chest electrodes each beat
QRS amplitude and axis alternate on consecutive complexes
Alternans with tachycardia prompts urgent tamponade assessment

steps.say: The chest film only turns flask shaped once a teacupful of fluid has gathered, so a normal film never rules out tamponade.
steps.tx: Radiography needs volume for the **water-bottle heart (water bottle sign)**. A symmetrical, globular, water bottle appearance on chest radiograph requires at least **200-250 mL** of pericardial fluid to manifest in older children, and echocardiography remains mandatory because haemodynamic collapse precedes radiographic change.

rows: Tamponade still possible by echo criteria
Large effusion with clear radiographic flag
Small volume tamponade after trauma or procedure

steps.say: Draining the sac is done through a needle slipped beneath the breastbone, watched every millimetre by ultrasound and the ECG.
steps.tx: Rescue is **emergency pericardiocentesis (echo guided)**. Pericardiocentesis via the subxiphoid approach (beneath the xiphisternum angled toward the left shoulder) under continuous echocardiographic and ECG monitoring is life saving in cardiac tamponade, with ST elevation on the needle ECG warning of myocardial contact.

left.title: Subxiphoid Technique
points: Needle enters left of xiphisternum at 30 degrees to the skin
Aimed toward the left shoulder under continuous echo vision
ECG limb lead attached to needle detects epicardial touch

right.title: Monitoring During Drainage
points: Blood pressure and heart rate recover as fluid is aspirated
Agitated saline confirms intrapericardial needle position
Pigtail catheter left for slow or recurrent collections

steps.say: The ECG of acute pericarditis evolves through stages, and stage one has a signature every student must recognise on sight.
steps.tx: Early changes define **stage one acute pericarditis ECG stages**. Stage one ECG in acute pericarditis shows diffuse concave ST elevation with PR depression across limb and precordial leads, except aVR and V1 which show PR elevation, a pattern distinguishing pericarditis from territorial ST elevation infarction.

nodes.label: Diffuse concave ST elevation across most leads with PR segment depression
Leads aVR and V1 paradoxically show PR elevation instead
ST segments normalize over days then T waves invert diffusely
No pathological Q waves or reciprocal changes unlike infarction

steps.say: Most children recover fully on anti inflammatory medicines alone, with a second drug added specifically to stop the illness coming back.
steps.tx: Treatment is **medical therapy for acute pericarditis**. First line medical treatment of acute idiopathic or viral pericarditis combines NSAIDs (ibuprofen) with weight adjusted colchicine for **3 months** to prevent recurrences, adding exercise restriction and proton protection until inflammation markers and echo normalize.
